study.question: Does replacing the latest other-field match anchor with its complete empirical age distribution add predictive information to the required-support crossed order feature, and is any effect specific to raw order rather than averaging decay? Observation: r0013-required_rank has AUC 0.6198327315 / Logloss 0.1959002720, versus required_presence 0.6194625510 / 0.1959638715 and common-rank r0012-crossed_rank 0.6196262013 / 0.1959319579. The exact source uses only minimum match age; it discards all other matching ages in the added comparison. Source-checked candidate diagnostics on 512 impressions show required support 0.15576171875 versus common 0.076171875 and brand/pv required support 0.65234375. Multiple-anchor prevalence is currently unmeasured. These are observations and a code limitation, not evidence that the discarded ages improve outcomes.
study.hypothesis: Conditional on the same crossed populations, comparing every receiving-field nonmatch with every other-field target match captures persistent temporal separation that a single most recent match cannot represent. This is an information-aggregation hypothesis, with provisional robustness-to-one-recent-match interpretation. Prediction: all_rank exceeds latest_rank in full validation AUC, with a larger aggregation effect for raw rank than decay. Earlier success of latest extrema is counterevidence to indiscriminate averaging; this replacement may fail.

study.proposed_difference: Let N_f,a be known-target nonmatching event ages in receiving field f for action a and M_other,a be matching ages in the other field. Preserve g=1[|N|>0 and |M|>0]. latest/rank is g*mean_n(1[n<min(M)]+0.5*1[n=min(M)]), exactly the incumbent. all/rank is g*mean_(n,m)(1[n<m]+0.5*1[n=m]). latest/decay is g*(0.5+0.5*(mean_n d(n)-d(min(M)))); all/decay substitutes mean_m d(m), where d(t)=exp(-ln(2)*t/86400). Same eight bounded coordinates, same support, capacity, initialization and data. Compute all summaries in each variant. Pairwise order is evaluated by sorted ages, tie-aware lower/upper boundaries and cumulative nonmatch counts, O(B*L*log L + B*L*actions*fields) time / O(B*L*actions) auxiliary storage, with no L-by-L pair tensor. This is a conventional empirical pairwise rank construction, not a mathematical novelty claim. Registry searches for sequence/temporal distribution work found no additional verified primary method; closest external search is limited and priority remains unverified.
predictions: Predeclared primary: AUC(all_rank)-AUC(latest_rank)>0 on the same full validation population under the frozen recipe. Report Logloss and all cost metrics even if discordant.
Predeclared attribution: interaction [AUC(all_rank)-AUC(latest_rank)]-[AUC(all_decay)-AUC(latest_decay)]>0. No formal statistical significance is claimed from these single-seed point estimates.

Mechanism diagnostics: identical required gates in all cells; all/rank equals latest/rank when anchor count is one (or all anchor ages equal); all/rank>=latest/rank on support, with strict differences possible only for multiple distinct anchor ages. Measure support, multiple-anchor prevalence and feature/logit gaps, without treating coordinate use as proof of benefit.

Exploratory slices use only host pre-existing bins: history length/empty, hour, behavior presence, target-category match and training frequency. Always retain sample/positive/negative counts. Multiple-anchor-specific AUC cannot be measured unless the host exposes that slice; do not infer it from 512 label-free diagnostics.
falsifiers: If all_rank fails to beat latest_rank, the proposed persistent-distribution predictor is not locally supported in this implementation. Do not substitute a favorable slice for the primary result.
If aggregation improves decay as much as rank or more, the raw-order-specific explanation is unsupported; generic averaging or recency scale remains plausible.

If multiple-anchor support is absent/negligible or all/latest summaries coincide, this dataset view cannot meaningfully test the distribution mechanism. If all_rank improves only where expected features should be identical, inspect shared-training effects and seed variability before attribution.
Any support, singleton, tie, padding, permutation or finite-output violation invalidates mechanism interpretation; retain failed cost and repair only within the same information contract.

A single favorable seed is preliminary. A later frozen paired-seed comparison failing to maintain the contrast defeats repeated-support claims. Source priority/novelty stays unverified regardless of local performance.

Changing aggregation changes the feature scale/distribution and sensitivity to old events; it does not isolate noise robustness from temporal relevance.
Upstream counts may indirectly encode support; zero rank versus missing support remains ambiguous and is not repaired here.

Equal model capacity/data passes do not ensure equal measured GPU or wall cost; historical incumbent omits new sorting overhead.
Latest events may carry the strongest intent, consistent with r0010/r0011; averaging stale matches can erase useful change signals.
Any gain may reflect smoothing, changed coordinate scale or easier optimization rather than robustness or persistent preference. No causal preference or negative-interest claim is made.

Adaptive selection over many previous rounds may produce optimism; paired seeds quantify initialization variation but do not undo validation reuse. User-cluster bootstrap and new independent data are unavailable in this coding phase.
